advances:
For every prescribed \(a_1,a_2,a_3>0\), the minimum of
\[
\left|\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3)\right|
\]
over compact convex \(K_i\subseteq\overline{Q_i}\) containing \(0\) and satisfying \(|K_i|=a_i\) is attained by a triangle. Its three vertices can be assigned one to each \(\overline{Q_i}\), and its intersections with the selected sectors have exactly the prescribed areas. Thus the positive-area alternating-cone inequality, including its equality cases, reduces without loss to the terminal triangle calculation. If some \(a_i=0\), the desired inequality already follows directly.
author: mp_r41_fan_variation
proof:
The class \(\mathcal F(a_1,a_2,a_3)\) is nonempty, since a sufficiently scaled triangle with one vertex at \(0\) can be placed in each selected sector.

We first prove compactness of minimizing sequences. Let
\[
H_n=\operatorname{conv}(K_{1,n}\cup K_{2,n}\cup K_{3,n})
\]
be a minimizing sequence with \(|H_n|\le M_0\). Suppose that \(D_n=\operatorname{diam}(H_n)\to\infty\). Let \(L_n\) be a line through two points of \(H_n\) at distance \(D_n\), and let \(e_n\) be a unit direction vector of \(L_n\). For every \(z\in H_n\), the triangle with base the diameter segment and third vertex \(z\) lies in \(H_n\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z,L_n)\le \frac{2M_0}{D_n}.
\]
Since \(0\in H_n\), the whole body lies in a strip about the line through \(0\) parallel to \(e_n\), of total width at most \(4M_0/D_n\).

Let \(L_{i,n}\) be the length of the orthogonal projection of \(K_{i,n}\) onto \(\mathbb Re_n\). The strip bound gives
\[
a_i\le \frac{4M_0}{D_n}L_{i,n},
\qquad
L_{i,n}\ge \frac{a_iD_n}{4M_0}.
\]
Because \(0\in K_{i,n}\), there is \(z_{i,n}\in K_{i,n}\) with
\[
|z_{i,n}\cdot e_n|\ge \frac{a_iD_n}{8M_0}.
\]
Its component perpendicular to \(e_n\) is \(O(D_n^{-1})\). After taking a subsequence, \(e_n\) converges projectively to a line direction \(e\), and for every \(i\), one of the two directions \(\pm e\) belongs to \(\overline{Q_i}\). This is impossible: the three projective arcs
\[
\overline{Q_i\cup(-Q_i)}
\]
are the three distinct closed intervals cut out on the projective line by the original three line directions, and their triple intersection is empty. Thus the diameters are uniformly bounded.

Compact convex subsets of a fixed ball have a Hausdorff-convergent subsequence, as follows directly from compactness of their support functions. Passing to a common subsequence gives \(K_{i,n}\to K_i\). Planar area is continuous under Hausdorff convergence of bounded convex bodies, by sandwiching between inner and outer parallel bodies. Convex hull also commutes with this convergence. Hence \(|K_i|=a_i\), and the limiting triple attains \(M(a_1,a_2,a_3)\).

Fix a minimizing triple and write
\[
H=\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3).
\]
We next prove saturation:
\[
K_i=H\cap\overline{Q_i}. \tag{1}
\]
Certainly \(K_i\subseteq H\cap\overline{Q_i}\). Put \(A_i=|H\cap Q_i|\). Suppose \(A_i>a_i\), and set
\[
\lambda=\sqrt{\frac{a_i}{A_i}}<1,
\qquad
\widetilde K_i=\lambda(H\cap\overline{Q_i}),
\qquad
\widetilde K_j=K_j\quad(j\ne i).
\]
Then \(|\widetilde K_i|=a_i\), so the new triple is feasible, and its hull \(\widetilde H\) is contained in \(H\).

There is a linear functional \(\varphi_i\), supplied by the third fan line, which is negative on \(Q_i\) and nonnegative on \(Q_j\cup Q_k\). Since \(a_i>0\),
\[
m:=\min_H\varphi_i<0.
\]
For the new hull,
\[
\min_{\widetilde H}\varphi_i=\lambda m>m.
\]
Thus \(\widetilde H\) is a proper closed convex subset of \(H\). Since \(H\) has nonempty interior, the strict support gap removes a positive-area cap, so \(|\widetilde H|<|H|\), contradicting minimality. Therefore \(A_i=a_i\). Inclusion and equality of the positive areas of the two compact convex sets imply (1).

Every extreme point of \(H\) belongs to \(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3\): otherwise a Carathéodory representation of that point by points of this compact union would express it as a nontrivial convex combination. Hence no open intervening sector contains an extreme point of \(H\). The boundary of \(H\) across each intervening sector is therefore a straight bridge segment.

Number the fan rays cyclically so that \(Q_i\) lies between the rays containing \(A_i\) and \(B_i\), and the bridge after \(Q_i\) joins \(B_i\) to \(A_{i+1}\). Here the same letters denote the nonzero intersections of the rays with \(\partial H\). The selected boundary arc from \(A_i\) to \(B_i\) can be replaced by one vertex without changing its sector area.

Indeed, the lines containing the preceding and following bridge segments are supporting lines of \(H\). Unless the selected arc is already the chord \([A_i,B_i]\), these lines meet at a point \(U_i\) on the exterior side of the chord. Convexity gives
\[
H\cap Q_i
\subseteq
\operatorname{conv}\{0,A_i,U_i,B_i\}.
\]
The parallel case can only occur when the intervening boundary is collinear, because the oriented boundary direction of a convex body is monotone; it is therefore already the chord case. Put
\[
m_i=\frac12\det(A_i,B_i),
\qquad
M_i=\frac12\bigl(\det(A_i,U_i)+\det(U_i,B_i)\bigr).
\]
With the counterclockwise orientation, \(m_i\le a_i\le M_i\). Choose any \(D_i\in[A_i,B_i]\) and
\[
s_i=\frac{a_i-m_i}{M_i-m_i},
\qquad
V_i=(1-s_i)D_i+s_iU_i
\]
when \(a_i>m_i\). Linearity of the determinant gives
\[
\frac12\bigl(\det(A_i,V_i)+\det(V_i,B_i)\bigr)=a_i.
\]
The path through \(A_i,V_i,B_i\) remains convex because \(V_i\) lies in the triangle bounded by the chord and the two adjacent supporting lines. When \(a_i=m_i\), omit \(V_i\) and use the chord. Doing this independently in the three selected sectors leaves all bridge segments and all six sector areas unchanged. It produces another minimizer \(P\), now a polygon whose only possible vertices are
\[
A_i,\quad V_i,\quad B_i\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]

We now eliminate all extra fan-ray vertices by exact area-preserving variations. Write \([X,Y]=\det(X,Y)\).

First suppose
\[
E_i:=2a_i-[A_i,B_i]>0.
\]
Then \(V_i\) is present and is a strict vertex. Consider the right ray point \(B=B_i\), with \(A=A_i\), \(V=V_i\), and let \(C=A_{i+1}\) be the other endpoint of the following bridge. If \(B\) is a strict polygon vertex, put
\[
B_\lambda=\lambda B,
\qquad
V_\lambda=A+\sigma_\lambda(V-A),
\qquad 0<\lambda<1,
\]
where
\[
\sigma_\lambda=
\frac{2a_i-\lambda[A,B]}
{[A,V]+\lambda\bigl([V,B]-[A,B]\bigr)}. \tag{2}
\]
At \(\lambda=1\), the numerator and denominator in (2) both equal \(E_i\), so \(\sigma_1=1\). Moreover,
\[
\sigma_\lambda'
\big|_{\lambda=1}
=
-\frac{[V,B]}{E_i}<0.
\]
Thus \(\sigma_\lambda>1\) for \(\lambda<1\) sufficiently close to \(1\). Direct substitution in (2) gives
\[
[A,V_\lambda]+[V_\lambda,B_\lambda]=2a_i,
\]
so the selected area is unchanged. The preceding turn at \(A\) is unchanged up to the positive factor \(\sigma_\lambda\), and the strict turns at \(V\) and \(B\) remain positive by continuity.

Only the turn at \(C\) requires attention. If it is strict, continuity suffices. If it is flat and \(W\) is the boundary point after \(C\), then
\[
W-C=\tau(C-B)
\]
for some \(\tau>0\). Hence
\[
[C-B_\lambda,W-C]
=
(1-\lambda)\tau[B,C]>0.
\]
Thus the perturbed polygon is convex. Its following bridge area changes from \([B,C]/2\) to \(\lambda[B,C]/2\), while every selected area and every other bridge area is unchanged. This contradicts minimality. Therefore, whenever \(E_i>0\), neither \(A_i\) nor \(B_i\) is a strict polygon vertex. The only strict vertex contributed by that selected sector is \(V_i\).

It remains to treat \(E_i=0\). Then the selected boundary is the chord \([A_i,B_i]\). Suppose both endpoints \(A=A_i\) and \(B=B_i\) are strict vertices. Choose \(D=(1-r)A+rB\) with \(0<r<1\), and set
\[
A_\lambda=\lambda A,
\qquad
B_\lambda=\lambda B,
\qquad
V_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}D.
\]
Then
\[
[A_\lambda,V_\lambda]+[V_\lambda,B_\lambda]
=
[A,D]+[D,B]
=
[A,B]
=
2a_i.
\]
Thus the selected area is preserved exactly. The new vertex \(V_\lambda\) lies strictly outside the chord \([A_\lambda,B_\lambda]\), since the chord area has fallen to \(\lambda^2a_i\). The turns at \(A\) and \(B\) are positive for \(\lambda<1\) close to \(1\), because at \(\lambda=1\) they are respectively \(r\) and \(1-r\) times the original strict turns.

The preceding and following bridge areas are both multiplied by \(\lambda\). At their remote endpoints, strict turns persist. A flat remote turn becomes strict: for example, if \(P\) is the preceding bridge endpoint, \(W\) precedes \(P\), and
\[
A-P=\tau(P-W),
\]
then
\[
[P-W,A_\lambda-P]
=
-(1-\lambda)[P-W,A]
=
\frac{1-\lambda}{\tau}[P,A]>0.
\]
The calculation at the following remote endpoint is identical. Hence this is a convex area-preserving perturbation which strictly lowers the total area, again contradicting minimality. Therefore, when \(E_i=0\), at most one of \(A_i,B_i\) is a strict polygon vertex.

We can now count vertices. Each selected sector contributes at most one strict vertex:

\[
E_i>0:\quad V_i\text{ is the only possible strict vertex},
\]
\[
E_i=0:\quad \text{at most one of }A_i,B_i\text{ is strict}.
\]
There are no vertices in the interiors of the bridge sectors. Thus \(P\) has at most three strict vertices. Since \(P\) has positive area, it has at least three strict vertices. It therefore has exactly three and is a triangle. Equality in the count also assigns one of its vertices to each \(\overline{Q_i}\). By construction,
\[
|P\cap Q_i|=a_i,
\qquad
|P|=M(a_1,a_2,a_3).
\]
This proves the positive-area reduction.

Finally, suppose at least one \(a_i\) is zero. There are at most two positive areas. Distinct selected sectors have disjoint interiors, so
\[
|H|\ge \sum_i a_i.
\]
For at most two positive numbers,
\[
\frac12\left(\sum_i\sqrt{a_i}\right)^2
\le \sum_i a_i
\]
by \(2\sqrt{a_ia_j}\le a_i+a_j\). If exactly two areas are positive, convexity between interior disks in the two separated sectors adds a positive-area bridge outside their union, so \(|H|>\sum_i a_i\). With exactly one positive area, the displayed square-root bound is already strict. If all three areas vanish, equality holds exactly when \(|H|=0\).
statement:
Let three distinct lines through \(0\) divide \(\mathbb R^2\) into six sectors, and let \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) be alternate sectors. For \(a_1,a_2,a_3>0\), let \(\mathcal F(a_1,a_2,a_3)\) be the set of triples of compact convex sets \(K_i\subseteq\overline{Q_i}\) containing \(0\), with \(|K_i|=a_i\). Put
\[
M(a_1,a_2,a_3)
=
\inf_{(K_1,K_2,K_3)\in\mathcal F(a_1,a_2,a_3)}
\left|\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3)\right|.
\]
Then the infimum is attained. Moreover, there is a minimizing triangle \(T\) containing \(0\) such that
\[
|T\cap Q_i|=a_i\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\]
and \(T\) has one vertex in each \(\overline{Q_i}\).

Consequently, proving
\[
|T|\ge
\frac12\left(\sqrt{|T\cap Q_1|}
+\sqrt{|T\cap Q_2|}
+\sqrt{|T\cap Q_3|}\right)^2
\]
for these triangles proves the alternating-cone hull inequality for all positive-area compact convex pieces.

If at least one \(a_i\) is zero, then
\[
\left|\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3)\right|
\ge
\frac12\left(\sqrt{a_1}+\sqrt{a_2}+\sqrt{a_3}\right)^2.
\]
This inequality is strict unless all \(a_i=0\) and the hull has zero area.
